title: Despotate of Vidin
capsule: The Despotate of Vidin was a semi-autonomous Bulgarian principality centered on the Danube fortress city of Vidin, carved out after the fragmentation of the Second Bulgarian Empire; Ivan Stratsimir governed it from around 1356 as son of Tsar Ivan Alexander. Following a Hungarian occupation (1365–1369), Stratsimir recovered Vidin with Ottoman backing and ruled as a client of Sultan Murad I and subsequently Bayezid I. The principality was extinguished when Ivan Stratsimir was captured after the catastrophic Christian defeat at the Battle of Nicopolis on 25 September 1396, and Bayezid I annexed Vidin directly into the Ottoman Empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political outline of the Despotate of Vidin is reasonably attested through Bulgarian, Byzantine, and Ottoman sources, but its precise territorial extent within the 1363–1402 window is uncertain and reconstructed from incomplete medieval records complicated by the Hungarian interlude.
